TYRES ARE BLACK IN THE SHIPPED ASSET - resolved, not assumed. The wheel-ring geometry (4 primitives sitting on the ground plane) binds to 'Gar_p4b', which is textured; its baseColorTexture was extracted from the GLB by HTTP Range and is a 1024x1024 Pirelli P Zero tread-and-sidewall map at mean RGB 27.5. NOTE this overturns my own first reading, which took the black 'Gar_gum' (baseColor 0.05) for the tyre - Gar_gum starts 9% of body height ABOVE the ground, so it is seal/trim rubber, not the tyre.

the white tyres in the sheet are the render worker's doing: a red control render returned recolour.materials = [Gar_alu, Gar_chr, Gar_gum, Gar_kob, Gar_lac, Gar_skl, Gar_vbl, Gar_voy, JXF2_lak, JXF2_tex] - TEN of the 14 materials treated as body, including the tyre rubber and the glass. In red the whole car including glass and tyres goes red.
door and bonnet shut lines defined; grille mesh and lamp internals present; UK number-plate texture present

PUBLISHING CAVEAT: cov=0.957 puts this in the documented cov>0.90 bucket - a render-time respray repaints glass and tyres with the body (toyota-auris-v1 was retired for exactly this). colour_variants.py edits named materials and is a different mechanism, so it may still be fine, but this car must not ship a colour variant without recolour_audit --stamp.
